author: blu
body: This used to require a letter or digit AFTER the hyphen, which made `a-` impossible and left `a- 2` lexing as subtraction. Four spacings then had three meanings instead of four, and the missing one is the one a reader assumes.

author: blu
body: The single exception is `->`. A hyphen before `>` is the arrow, not a name character, and consuming it here would turn `a->b` into `a-` `>` `b`. The operator scanner makes the same exception a few hundred lines below. The old `--` case is gone because it no longer needs saying: the first hyphen is consumed, the second is consumed, and a name like `a--b` falls out of the general rule.

author: blu
body: The ceiling is the LEX deck reservation's top, and it is checked here because this loop is the only place the phase writes the deck in bulk: every token puts its kind there, and the linked list threading them sits in the bivy immediately above the reservation. Past the ceiling the deck grows into that list and the lexer reads its own overwrite, which is a #GP in __linked_list_to_list with nothing said -- the phase's own check-deck-overflow runs after the phase and never arrives. A ceiling of zero means unbounded, which is what a caller with no reservation of its own passes.
